item.title: Can These Bones Live? Ezekiel 35-37, Job 13, John 11, 1 John 3
item.description:
John 11:1-16, 1 John 3:1-10, Job 13, Ezekiel 35-37
Ezekiel preaches to a valley of dry bones, and God promises a new heart and his own Spirit for the sake of his name. Job says, though he slay me, I will hope in him, Jesus waits two days because he loves Lazarus, and John marvels that we are called children of God. With Matthew Henry, Tertullian, Spurgeon, Calvin, Chrysostom, Thomas Watson, Augustine, and Ligonier. item.title: Human Sheep of My Pasture: Ezekiel 33-34, Job 12, John 10, 1 John 2
item.description:
John 10:22-42, 1 John 2:24-29, Job 12, Ezekiel 33-34
Ezekiel's mouth is opened when the fugitive arrives with news that Jerusalem has fallen, and God turns from the shepherds who fed themselves to the one shepherd, his servant David. With Job's reply to Zophar, Jesus at the Feast of Dedication, and John's call to abide, with Calvin, Henry, Spurgeon, Gregory, Augustine and Chrysostom. item.title: Whom Are You Like? Ezekiel 31-32, Job 11, John 10, 1 John 2
item.description:
John 10:11-21, 1 John 2:18-23, Job 11, Ezekiel 31-32
Ezekiel holds up fallen Assyria as a towering cedar to warn Pharaoh, then sings Egypt down into the pit with the uncircumcised. Is that a map of the afterlife? Plus Zophar's true words at the wrong bedside, the good shepherd who lays down his life and takes it up again, and John's 'last hour'. item.title: My Nile Is My Own: Ezekiel 29-30, Job 10, John 10, 1 John 2
item.description:
John 10:1-10, 1 John 2:12-17, Job 10, Ezekiel 29-30
Pharaoh lies in the Nile like a crocodile and says, My Nile is my own; I made it, while Judah leans on Egypt like a reed that snaps. We face the strange verse where Nebuchadnezzar gets no wages for Tyre, hear Job speak straight to his Maker, walk through the low door of John 10, and learn from First John what it means not to love the world. item.title: In the Heart of the Seas: Ezekiel 27-28, Job 9, John 9, 1 John 2
item.description:
John 9:26-41, 1 John 2:1-11, Job 9:21-35, Ezekiel 27-28
Tyre sinks in the heart of the seas: Ezekiel's funeral song for a merchant ship-city and the king who said 'I am a god', and the old debate over whether Ezekiel 28 describes Satan's fall, with Tertullian, Augustine, Gregory, Henry, Keil and Carson. Job cries for an arbiter, the healed blind man is cast out and found, and 1 John answers Job with an advocate and a propitiation for the whole world (Calvin, Owen, Spurgeon). item.title: The Delight of Your Eyes: Ezekiel 24-26, Job 9, John 9, 1 John 1
item.description:
John 9:13-25, 1 John 1:5-10, Job 9:1-20, Ezekiel 24-26
The siege of Jerusalem begins, Ezekiel's wife, the delight of his eyes, dies, and he is told not to mourn, while Tyre gloats over Jerusalem's fall. Job asks how a man can be in the right before God, the man born blind faces the Pharisees with 'One thing I do know', and John tells us that God is light and faithful and just to forgive. item.description:
John 8:21-30, 2 Peter 2:17-22, Job 5, Ezekiel 16
Ezekiel 16 tells the story of a baby left to die in a field, the God who said 'Live!', and a bride who gave his gifts to her lovers. It ends with an everlasting covenant and an atonement she never paid for. item.title: Unless: Lamentations 4-5, Song of Songs 8, John 7, 1 Peter 5
item.description:
John 7:25-36, 1 Peter 5:8-14, Song of Songs 8:8-14, Lamentations 4-5

item.description:
John 7:14-24, 1 Peter 5:1-7, Song of Songs 8:1-7, Lamentations 3
At the center of Lamentations a broken man remembers something, and the darkest poem in the book turns into 'great is your faithfulness.' We work through who 'the man' is, how God can afflict 'not from his heart' and still rule all things, then climb to the summit of the Song of Songs, hear Jesus teach without credentials at the Feast of Booths, and listen to Peter tell elders how to shepherd and all of us how to cast our anxieties on God. item.title: Torn Scroll, Untorn Robes: Jeremiah 35-38, Ecclesiastes 11, John 4, 1 Peter 1
item.description:
John 4:43-54, 1 Peter 1:10-16, Ecclesiastes 11, Jeremiah 35-38
Jehoiakim cut Jeremiah's scroll column by column and burned it, yet no one in the room tore his robe. We go deeper into the Rechabites, then follow Jeremiah through the burned scroll, the dungeon, and the muddy cistern, and ask whether he lied to Zedekiah's officials. Also Ecclesiastes 11 on sowing without knowing, the official who believed Jesus' word in John 4, and the prophets who served us in 1 Peter 1.
